subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation (Parkwell Health)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation (Parkwell Health)

Hi Amanda —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Repeated model-serving incidents over the last 9 months (notably Apr and Jun) causing user-facing latency spikes and a 2 hour partial outage in Apr that affected synchronous workflows.
- Lack of automated graceful degradation: when preferred model or region is saturated the app currently returns errors instead of falling back to a cheaper/model variant or other region.
- Need for predictable end-to-end latency for triage workflows (95th percentile target ~350ms for short prompts).
- Procurement/security requirements: SOC 2 evidence, IP/data residency concerns, and audit logs for model inputs.

Current stack you described:
- Frontend app + backend in GCP (us-west1 primary)
- Batch jobs on-prem for nightly syncs
- Using a mix of small open models run in-house and a managed API for peak traffic

Success criteria (what Parkwell needs to consider a win):
1) Incidents like Apr/Jun are prevented or limited by automated fallback policies (failover to secondary region or fallback model within < 90s).
2) 95th percentile latency for short interactive prompts <= 350ms under normal load and recovery modes <= 800ms.
3) Clear audit trail: per-request logs retained 90+ days for initial evaluation (configurable).
4) Predictable unit cost at scale with recommendations for batching/caching to avoid cost surprises.

Options we discussed for graceful degradation and reliability:
- Multi-region routing with automatic failover (primary us-west1, failover us-east1) and canary rollouts to catch regressions.
- Model-variant fallbacks: route to a quantized/optimized variant when primary model is saturated; we can provide verified performance profiles for each variant.
- Prefix/KV caching to reduce load on upstream model for repeated prompts.
- SLO monitoring + automatic route diversion when SLOs breach; alerting + runbook integration.

Risks / open questions you asked us to confirm:
- Expected failover time between regions (our target is configurable; default warm-up + failover < 60-120s depending on cold-starts; we will quantify on the technical deep dive).
- Whether fallbacks preserve functional parity (we'll provide evals/quality delta for suggested model variants).
- Data residency — we can keep inference in your VPC or enforce region-only routing for Private deployments.

Next steps (agreed):
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/ops team — propose Thu Aug 6 @ 10:00am PT. (Jonas will bring the latency/failover playbook.)
2) I’ll share: SOC 2 overview, mutual action plan (MAP), and a short doc listing fallback model variants + perf profiles.
3) Parkwell to share incident post-mortem for Apr outage and a single example trace of a degraded call so we can reproduce.

Attachments: SOC2_overview.pdf (brief), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MAP draft).

Thanks again – excited to scope this with your team.

– Ben
